back: An animal, body part or object adopted as the symbol of a clan, usually passed from father to children.
A further name within a totem identifying a particular branch of the clan.
Poetic praises naming the totem, ancestors and clan history, recited to thank, honour or comfort.
The study and record of a family's line of descent, often shown as a family tree.

front: Whose totem does a child take? Does a wife change hers?
back: The father's. No: a married woman keeps her own totem.

front: Why do totems discourage marriage between people of the same totem?
back: They are regarded as relatives descended from one ancestor, so the rule prevents incest and keeps family lines healthy.
Clan members do not kill or eat their totem animal, which protects it.

front: Name six purposes of the totem system.
back: Identity, preventing marriage between relatives, conservation, unity and hospitality, respect and social order, link with ancestors.
